memory_candidates.content: When writing a shell wrapper meant to be non-fatal (always return 0) around an external command invocation, the invocation itself MUST be inside an if/else (or otherwise protected from `set -e`), not just followed by `rc=$?`. Under `set -e` (or `set -euo pipefail`), a bare `cmd; rc=$?` still aborts the script the instant `cmd` exits non-zero -- the `rc=$?` line is never reached. Pattern: `if cmd; then rc=0; else rc=$?; fi` instead of `cmd; rc=$?`. This bug is easy to miss because it only manifests when the wrapped command actually fails, and tests that only exercise the present/absent-helper path (not the present-but-failing path) won't catch it.

For a doc-lint/gate script that must surface a KNOWN, currently-expected, user-gated condition (e.g. deploy drift that only a manual regeneration step can fix) without breaking every caller's existing pass/fail verdict -- especially when concurrent/sibling processes rely on the same gate for unrelated validation -- implement an ADVISORY lane, not a hard FAIL: a separate counter and always-visible summary section (deliberately ignoring --quiet) that never affects the exit code by default, plus an opt-in env-var (e.g. STRICT_CORE_DEPLOY=1) that promotes the same detections to real failures for callers who explicitly want the stricter gate (e.g. a post-fix verification run). This avoids the false choice between 'invisible' (silent info-skip) and 'blocks everyone' (hard FAIL).

For cross-repo event/log federation where a 'repo' identifier is derived from a stored working-directory path (cwd), prefer a pure computation (e.g. basename(cwd) via jq) over shelling out to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` per row when the consuming query tool already does native streaming jq filtering with no per-row subprocess spawns. This keeps performance characteristics unchanged and avoids introducing a git dependency into a log-query path; document the simplification explicitly so a future reader doesn't assume 'repo' means 'verified git toplevel'.
